note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Perform testing on complex electrical installation

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why is a written test plan needed before testing a building with several boards, a generator and a PV system?
options: So the team can do the tests in whatever order they like on the day itself
It sets the order, isolation points, instruments and expected results
So the client does not have to be told when the testing will happen
It replaces the need for any test certificates at the end of the job

questions.stem: A board can be fed from the mains, a generator and a PV inverter. Before dead testing, what must be done?
options: Isolate only the mains, since it is by far the largest source
Switch the generator to manual, then start testing straight away
Turn off the inverter's display screen so it shows nothing
Isolate and lock off every source, then prove dead at the work

questions.stem: Why must the tester check for back-feed before working on a board supplied through a UPS?
options: The UPS can keep the outgoing side live from its batteries
The UPS makes the board run at a higher supply frequency
The UPS always switches its batteries off when mains fails
The UPS trips the mains breaker every time that it starts

questions.stem: During an insulation test on a long sub-main cable, the reading keeps rising for a minute or more. Why?
options: The tester's battery gets stronger as the tester itself warms up
The cable is drying out because of the test voltage
The cable charges up and the absorption current falls away
The cable's copper shrinks as it is heated by the test

questions.stem: A motor's insulation reads 400 MΩ at 1 minute and 1 000 MΩ at 10 minutes. What is its polarisation index?
A large motor gives a polarisation index of 1.0, although its 1-minute reading is above the minimum. What does this suggest?
options: The windings may be damp or dirty, so look into it first
The insulation is in excellent condition for a motor of its age
The tester was set to the wrong range for the motor
The motor has been running too fast for its rating

questions.stem: Why must the insulation test voltage suit the circuit and the equipment being tested?
options: A higher test voltage always gives a more accurate reading
The lowest voltage is always chosen to save the battery
The test voltage sets the frequency the circuit runs at
Too low may miss faults; too high may damage equipment

questions.stem: A micro-ohm test across the busbar joints of a main switchboard reads 14, 16, 15 and 48 µΩ. What should be done?
options: Accept them all, because every one is far below 1 Ω
Retest only the joint with the lowest reading
Check and remake the 48 µΩ joint, then test it again
Paint every joint to keep corrosion away from the copper

questions.stem: Why does a micro-ohm meter pass a large DC current through a busbar joint?
options: To heat the joint so that it tightens itself up as it warms
So the tiny voltage across the joint can be read well
To trip the main breaker as one part of the test
To burn off any dust that has settled on the bars

questions.stem: Why does a micro-ohm meter use four leads, two for current and two for voltage?
options: So the resistance of the leads is left out of the result
So that two people can hold the leads at the same time
So that it can test two separate joints at exactly the same time
So that it can measure AC and DC together in one test

questions.stem: In a fall-of-potential test on an earth electrode, the current spike is 50 m away. Where is the potential spike usually placed first?
options: 5 m from the electrode
25 m from the electrode
50 m from the electrode
31 m from the electrode

questions.stem: In a fall-of-potential test, why are more readings taken with the potential spike moved a few metres each side of its first position?
options: To work out how deep the earth rod goes into the ground
To find out how long the test leads are from end to end
To see that the readings agree, so spacing is enough
To measure the temperature of the soil

questions.stem: With the building isolated, why is the main earth electrode disconnected from the installation before a fall-of-potential test?
options: So the tester can be powered from the building's supply
So parallel earth paths do not give a false low reading
So the rod can be pulled out of the ground and measured
So the earth tester can show its reading in kilohms

questions.stem: When is a clamp-on (stakeless) earth tester the right tool?
options: When the electrode is one of many in parallel on the system
When the building has one rod and no other earth path at all
When the rod is buried under concrete with no access to it
When the soil around the rod is completely dry, loose sand

questions.stem: A three-phase sub-main has L1, L2, L3, N and E. If every pair of conductors is insulation tested, how many tests is that?
On a 110/220 V split-phase board, why is it checked that each 110 V single-pole breaker is in a line conductor, not the neutral?
options: So the power company's meter records the right energy
So the 220 V circuits do not run at only half voltage
So opening the breaker makes the line conductor dead
So the RCD trips at a lower leakage current than usual

questions.stem: A circuit's loop impedance reads 0.6 Ω on the mains but 1.4 Ω on the standby generator. The maximum for its breaker is 1.1 Ω. What does this mean?
options: The circuit passes, because only the mains result counts
On the generator the breaker may not disconnect in time
The generator is faulty and must be replaced at once
The breaker should be changed for a larger rating

questions.stem: A phase rotation tester on a new three-phase sub-board shows L1-L3-L2. What does this mean?
options: The order is reversed, so three-phase motors would run backwards
The supply frequency is lower than the rated 50 Hz
The neutral is broken somewhere between the boards
The voltage on L2 is higher than on the other lines

questions.stem: A sub-board feeds speed drives and EV chargers. Why must the tester check the RCD type marked on each device?
options: Every type trips at the same current, so it makes no odds
The type decides the colour of the device's test button
Some loads leak DC, which a type AC RCD may not detect
The type tells the tester how many poles the device has

questions.stem: An upstream RCD is marked 'S' (time-delayed) and feeds 30 mA RCDs downstream. Why is it designed this way?
options: The S type always trips faster than the 30 mA devices
The S type is made only for use outdoors in the rain
The S type never needs to be tested once it is fitted
So a final-circuit fault trips only the 30 mA device

questions.stem: A board has a mechanical and electrical interlock between its mains and generator breakers. What must the functional test prove?
options: That both breakers can be closed together when it is needed
That the two breakers can never be closed at the same time
That the generator starts up by itself every hour
That the meter stops turning while the generator runs

questions.stem: A metering current transformer (CT) is rated 200/5 A. With 150 A in the primary, what should the secondary current be?
Why is the polarity of each CT (P1/P2 and S1/S2) checked on a three-phase energy meter?
options: The polarity sets the CT's ratio, such as 200/5
The polarity decides the CT's voltage rating
A reversed CT makes the meter read wrongly, even backwards
Polarity matters only on single-phase energy meters in houses

questions.stem: What does secondary injection testing of a protection relay prove?
options: That the insulation of the CT and its wiring is sound
That all the main busbar joints are tight and clean
That the breaker's handle moves freely
That the relay trips at its settings and times

questions.stem: What does primary injection testing prove that secondary injection does not?
options: That the display on the relay can be read easily
That the CT, its wiring and the relay work as a whole
That the circuit breaker has been painted in the right colour
That the main cable has been cut to the right length

questions.stem: Three identical PV strings of 12 modules read 452 V, 449 V and 411 V open circuit, measured within minutes of each other. What is the most likely fault?
options: A module missing, shorted or bypassed in the third string
The third string faces the sun more directly than the others
The inverter has been set to the wrong supply frequency
The first two strings have been charged up too much

questions.stem: Why is the polarity of each PV string checked before it is connected to the inverter?
options: A reversed string makes the panels much hotter in the sun
The inverter shows the wrong time if a string is reversed
A reversed string can damage the inverter or the combiner
Polarity matters only on PV systems that have batteries

questions.stem: Why is a PV string disconnected only after its DC isolator is opened and its current is proved to be zero with a DC clamp meter?
options: The clamp meter must be calibrated before every single use
The string voltage rises once its current has fallen to zero
The cable colours change when the cables carry a current
Breaking DC under load can draw an arc that keeps burning

questions.stem: Why is a PV string's measured short-circuit current compared with the value expected for the sunlight at that moment?
options: The current is the same in full sun and in heavy shade
The current rises and falls with the sunlight on the panels
The current depends only on the length of the string cable
The current can be measured properly only at night, in the dark

questions.stem: Phase rotation is correct on the mains supply to a three-phase board. Why is it checked again on the generator supply?
options: The generator always turns at a different speed from the mains
The test on the mains also checks the generator's fuel level
The generator's phases may be wired in a different order
The tester's battery must be checked on both of the supplies

questions.stem: Before insulation testing a motor cable fed from a variable speed drive, what must be done?
options: Disconnect the cable from the drive's output terminals
Leave the drive connected so that it is tested as well
Set the drive to its fastest speed before the test
Set the drive's display so that it shows the current

questions.stem: A steel-wire armoured cable's armour is used as its protective conductor. What should the test confirm?
options: The armour is painted all along its length
The armour is connected at the motor end only
The armour is kept isolated from each gland
It is continuous, with a suitable resistance

questions.stem: R1 + R2 readings for six identical lighting circuits are 0.42, 0.45, 0.44, 0.43, 1.85 and 0.44 Ω. What is the best action?
options: Accept them all, because every one of the readings is under 2 Ω
Look for a loose or poor joint on the 1.85 Ω circuit
Average them and record 0.67 Ω for every circuit
Replace the tester and start all the tests again

questions.stem: A micro-ohm meter passes 100 A DC through a busbar joint and reads 2.0 mV across it. What is the joint's resistance?
options: 2 µΩ
200 µΩ
20 µΩ
50 µΩ

questions.stem: Why does the tester note the air temperature and humidity on insulation test records for large equipment?
options: Readings change with heat and damp, so trends need them
The client is charged more for any testing done on humid days
The tester works properly only when it is above 30 °C
The weather decides which tester is used on the day

questions.stem: Who should sign the test certificate for a complex installation?
options: The accountant who keeps the books for the client
Any team member who held a test lead
The firm that hired out the test instruments
The competent person who did or led the tests

questions.stem: You supervise two testers on a large job. One writes 'OK' on the schedule instead of the readings. What should you do?
options: Accept it, as long as each of the circuits is working
Have the readings taken again and written as values
Fill in some typical values taken from another job
Leave those circuits off the schedule altogether

questions.stem: Why is the tester checked on a check box of known values before and after a day's testing?
options: To warm up the tester's battery before the day starts
To set the tester's clock to the right time and date
To show it read correctly for every test that day
To test the fuse inside the check box itself

questions.stem: Why must the tests on a complex installation follow the planned order, with dead tests before any live tests?
options: Dead tests find faults that would make live tests dangerous
Live tests are quicker, so they should always be done first of all
Dead tests are needed only on cables that are brand new
The order matters only for keeping the paperwork neat

questions.stem: Why is the insulation between neutral and earth tested on circuits protected by RCDs?
options: The neutral carries no current, so it can never fail at all
The test shows whether the RCD is the right type
The test sets the RCD's trip time for the circuit
A neutral-earth fault can trip an RCD for no clear reason

questions.stem: The prospective fault current measured at a sub-board is higher than the breaking capacity of its breakers. What should be done?
options: Report it to the designer, as the devices may need changing
Ignore it, because breakers hardly ever see a real fault
Fit larger cables to the board to bring the fault level down
Write the breaker rating on the sheet instead of the result

questions.stem: Before dead testing a sub-board in a busy hospital, what must the test plan arrange?
options: Testing at the busiest time, so the staff can watch the work
Switching off every circuit with no warning given
An agreed shutdown, with critical loads on another supply
Testing the board while it stays live throughout

questions.stem: What should the test records for a complex installation hold, so that later tests can be compared with them?
options: Only the word 'pass' written against each test
Readings, instrument, method, conditions and the circuit
The tester's own opinion of the whole installation
The price that was charged for each separate test on the job

questions.stem: Which is NOT a reason to test a complex installation after a major alteration?
options: To prove that the new work is safe to use
To check that existing circuits were not harmed
To record results to compare with in future
To find out which make of cable was used

questions.stem: The assessor's results sheet shows 2.5 A flowing in a building's main earthing conductor in normal use. What should the tester do?
options: Find where it comes from, such as a neutral-earth fault
Accept it, since earth conductors are meant to carry current
Cut the earthing conductor so that the current stops
Fit a larger main breaker so the current is shared

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the ratio of the 60-second insulation reading to the 30-second reading called? (words or letters)
A metering CT has a ratio of 400/5. What is that ratio as a single number?
Which RCD type (by letter) detects smooth DC earth leakage as well as AC?
On a current transformer, do the markings S1 and S2 show the primary or the secondary terminals?
A measured protective conductor resistance is 0.35 Ω. The design data says multiply by 1.2 to allow for working temperature. What is the corrected figure, in ohms?
On a Jamaican 110/220 V split-phase supply, what voltage should be measured between either line and the neutral?
A PV string has 12 modules in series, each with an open-circuit voltage of 38 V. What open-circuit voltage should the string have, in volts?
What is the test called that proves a system works as intended, such as an interlock or a changeover, rather than measuring a value? (one or two words)
Does an insulation resistance tester apply AC or DC to the circuit under test?
In PV testing, what do the letters Voc stand for?
What is it called when an inverter or generator keeps feeding a part of the grid that the power company has disconnected?
On a single-phase 110 V circuit with line, neutral and earth, how many insulation tests are needed to test every pair of conductors?
Five testers work on one isolated board. How many personal padlocks should be on its multi-lock hasp?
What is the record of each circuit's test readings, attached to the installation certificate, called?
What is the time an RCD takes to open during a test called? (two words)

essays.stem: You lead the testing of a new three-storey commercial building with a main switchboard, six sub-boards, a standby generator with a transfer switch, a UPS and a rooftop PV system. Describe how you would plan the testing.
essays.modelAnswer: I would gather the design: the single-line diagram, schedules, the specification's test limits and the makers' data for the generator, UPS, PV inverter and drives. I would list every source of supply and every point where it can be isolated, and write the isolation plan with lock-off points. I would set the order: inspection first, then dead tests on each board and circuit (continuity, insulation resistance, polarity and earth electrode), then live tests by a competent person (loop impedance, fault current and RCD tests), on mains and on the generator, then functional tests of the transfer switch, interlocks, UPS and PV. I would choose instruments with in-date calibration and the right category rating, and list which equipment must be disconnected before insulation testing. I would agree shutdowns with the client, assign the team and their roles, and prepare blank schedules for each board. The plan would include hold points where I check the results before the next stage starts.
markingPoints: Collects the design, test limits and makers' data
Lists all sources and plans isolation and lock-off
Sets a correct order: inspection, dead, live (on both supplies), functional
Chooses calibrated, suitable instruments and lists equipment to disconnect
Agrees shutdowns, assigns the team, prepares schedules and sets hold points

essays.stem: Explain how you would safely isolate a distribution board that can be fed from the mains, a standby generator, a UPS and a grid-tied PV inverter, before dead testing.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would study the single-line diagram and the labels on site, so I know every source that can feed the board. I would warn the client and the users and agree the shutdown. I would switch off the PV inverter and open its AC isolator, and remember that the DC side stays live in daylight. I would set the generator so it cannot start, for example by switching its controller to off and isolating its starting battery as the maker allows, and lock its breaker open. I would switch the UPS to its maintenance mode or shut it down, isolate its batteries as the maker says, and lock off its output. Then I would open and lock off the mains isolator. Every source gets a lock and a tag, with one padlock per team member on a multi-lock hasp. I would check the voltage tester on a proving unit, prove dead at the board on every conductor, then check the tester again. Only then does testing begin.
markingPoints: Identifies all sources from the diagram and labels, and agrees the shutdown
Isolates the PV inverter and treats its DC side as live
Stops the generator starting and locks its breaker
Isolates the UPS and its batteries as the maker says, then the mains
Locks and tags every source, and proves dead with a tester checked before and after

essays.stem: Explain how you would carry out and judge an insulation test on a large pump motor and its cable. Include the polarisation index, using readings of 300 MΩ at 1 minute and 900 MΩ at 10 minutes.
essays.modelAnswer: With the motor isolated, locked off and proved dead, I would disconnect the cable from the starter or drive so no electronics are in the test. I would choose the test voltage the specification and the motor maker give, and warn others to keep clear. I would test the cable and windings to earth, and between windings where they can be separated. A long cable and a large motor act like a capacitor, so the reading rises over time as the charging and absorption currents die away. That is why a timed test is useful. I would record the reading at 1 minute and at 10 minutes. The polarisation index is the 10-minute reading divided by the 1-minute reading: 900 ÷ 300 = 3. A figure of about 2 or more usually shows clean, dry insulation, while about 1 suggests damp or dirt. So this motor's insulation looks good. I would record the temperature and humidity, then discharge the windings before touching them.
markingPoints: Isolates, proves dead and disconnects electronics, and chooses the right test voltage
Explains why the reading rises (capacitance and absorption)
Defines PI as 10-minute ÷ 1-minute reading
Works out PI = 3 and judges it as good
Records conditions and discharges before touching

essays.stem: Describe how you would test a building's main earth electrode by the fall-of-potential method, and how you would know the result is sound.
essays.modelAnswer: With the installation isolated and locked off, I would disconnect the earthing conductor from the electrode at the test link, so the result is not lowered by parallel paths through the supply's earth, and put up a warning notice. I would drive the current spike well away from the electrode, for example 50 m, in a straight line, away from buried services. I would drive the potential spike between them, at about 62% of the distance, which is 31 m. I would connect the tester as the maker shows and take a reading. Then I would move the potential spike a few metres nearer and a few metres further, and take two more readings. If the three readings are close, the spikes are far enough apart and the result is sound. If they differ a lot, the current spike must go further out and the test is repeated. I would record the readings, the distances and the ground conditions, compare the result with the design value, and reconnect the earth before the supply is restored.
markingPoints: Isolates and disconnects the electrode at the test link, with a notice
Places the current spike well away and the potential spike at about 62%
Takes readings with the potential spike moved each side
Explains that agreeing readings show a sound result; moves the spike further if not
Records, compares with design and reconnects before restoring supply

essays.stem: Explain how you would test the busbar and large cable joints of a main switchboard with a micro-ohm meter, and how you would judge the results.
essays.modelAnswer: The switchboard must be isolated, locked off and proved dead, with the incoming supply isolated by the power company or the authorised person if needed. I would check the micro-ohm meter on its check resistor. It uses four leads: two pass a large DC current through the joint, and two measure the tiny voltage across it, so the leads' own resistance is left out. I would clean the test points, place the voltage leads either side of each joint, just inside the current leads, and take the reading, reversing the current if the meter allows to cancel any small voltages. I would test every similar joint in the same way. To judge the results, I would compare joints of the same size and type with each other and with the maker's figures. A joint reading much higher than the others, for example 48 µΩ where the rest read about 15 µΩ, points to a loose, dirty or corroded joint. It is remade to the maker's torque and retested, and all readings are recorded.
markingPoints: Isolates, locks off and proves dead, and checks the meter
Explains the four-lead method and why
Describes correct placing of leads and taking readings
Judges by comparing similar joints and the maker's figures
Remakes high joints to the maker's torque, retests and records

essays.stem: Describe the tests you would carry out on the DC side of a grid-tied PV system before it is connected to the inverter, and the safety precautions you would take.
essays.modelAnswer: PV modules make voltage whenever light falls on them, so the DC side can never be made fully dead in daylight. I would wear suitable PPE, use instruments rated for the DC voltage, keep the DC isolator and string fuses open, and never break a string under load, because a DC arc can keep burning. First I would inspect the array, cables, connectors and the earthing of the frames. I would test the continuity of the frame earthing. With the string isolated, I would check the polarity of each string with a meter, because a reversed string can damage the inverter. I would measure each string's open-circuit voltage and compare it with the expected value and with the other strings. I would measure the short-circuit current with a suitable tester and compare it with the value expected for the sunlight at that time. Insulation resistance is tested with the method the inverter and module makers allow. All readings, with the light level and temperature, are recorded.
markingPoints: Explains that PV is live in daylight and takes DC precautions
Inspects and tests frame earthing continuity
Checks string polarity
Measures and compares Voc and Isc against expected values
Insulation tests as the makers allow and records readings with conditions

essays.stem: Explain how the current transformer (CT) circuits for metering and protection on a large switchboard are tested before the board is put into service.
essays.modelAnswer: With the board isolated, I would first check that each CT's ratio and class on its nameplate match the design. I would check the wiring from each CT's S1 and S2 terminals to the meter or relay against the drawing, and that the secondary circuit is earthed at one point only. I would check that each CT's shorting link is in the right position. A CT secondary must never be left open while primary current flows, because a dangerous high voltage can appear. A ratio and polarity check confirms that each CT gives the right secondary current and is fitted the right way round, so the meter does not read wrongly or backwards. Secondary injection, from a test set into the relay's input, proves the relay trips at its settings and in the right time. Primary injection, passing a large test current through the primary, proves the whole chain of CT, wiring and relay works together. All results are recorded and the links left in their service position.
markingPoints: Checks ratio, class and wiring against the design, with single-point earthing
Checks shorting links and explains the open-secondary danger
Ratio and polarity check
Secondary injection proves the relay's settings and times
Primary injection proves the whole chain; records and restores links

essays.stem: The assessor's results for sub-board DB-2 are: circuit 1 Zs 0.95 Ω on mains and 1.6 Ω on generator (maximum 1.4 Ω); circuit 2 insulation 0.8 MΩ (minimum 1 MΩ); circuit 3 R1 + R2 1.6 Ω where similar circuits read about 0.5 Ω; circuit 4 RCD trip time 350 ms at rated current (maximum 300 ms); circuit 5 all within limits. Explain what each result means and what you would do.
essays.modelAnswer: Circuit 1 passes on the mains, but on the generator its loop impedance of 1.6 Ω is above the 1.4 Ω maximum, so the breaker may not disconnect fast enough during a fault while on generator. I would report it to the designer: RCD protection, a different device or a larger protective conductor may be needed. Circuit 2's insulation of 0.8 MΩ is below the 1 MΩ minimum, so it fails. I would keep it isolated, split the circuit to find the fault, such as damp in a box or a damaged cable, repair it and retest. Circuit 3's R1 + R2 of 1.6 Ω is about three times the similar circuits, which points to a loose or poor joint or a wrong cable. I would find and fix it, then retest continuity and loop impedance. Circuit 4's RCD took 350 ms, over the 300 ms limit, so the RCD fails and must be replaced and retested. Circuit 5 passes. Each failure is recorded, the board is not handed over until all are cleared, and the retest results are added to the schedule.
markingPoints: Circuit 1: fails on generator supply; refers to the designer for a remedy
Circuit 2: insulation below minimum; isolates, finds and repairs, retests
Circuit 3: high R1 + R2 suggests a poor joint; finds, fixes and retests
Circuit 4: RCD too slow; replaces and retests
Records failures, holds handover until cleared, and records retests

essays.stem: As the lead tester on a large job, explain how you would supervise a team of testers and make sure their results are reliable.
essays.modelAnswer: Before work starts I would brief the team on the test plan, the isolation points and the safety rules, and check that each person is competent for the tests I give them. I would issue calibrated instruments, and have each tester check their instrument on a check box before and after each day's work, and record it. I would make sure every circuit is isolated, locked off and proved dead before dead tests, with each member's own padlock. I would insist that actual readings are written, not 'OK' or ticks, along with the instrument used. I would check the schedules every day: looking for readings that are the same on circuits of very different lengths, results that do not fit the design, and gaps. Where something looks wrong, I would have the test repeated, sometimes witnessing it myself. Only competent people do live tests. At the end I would review all the schedules before signing the certificate, because my signature says the results are true.
markingPoints: Briefs the team and matches tasks to competence
Uses calibrated instruments checked before and after use
Enforces safe isolation with personal padlocks
Requires real readings and checks schedules daily for errors, repeating doubtful tests
Reviews all results before signing the certificate

essays.stem: Explain why testing circuits that feed variable speed drives, UPS units and other electronic equipment needs special care, and what you would do about it.
essays.modelAnswer: Electronic equipment can be damaged by the high DC voltage of an insulation test, and it can also give false low readings, because its filters and surge devices connect the conductors to earth. Speed drives and UPS units also hold stored energy in their capacitors after they are switched off, and a UPS can keep its output live from its batteries. So before testing I would read the makers' instructions. I would isolate, lock off and prove dead, wait the discharge time marked on the drive or UPS, and prove dead again. For insulation tests, I would disconnect the drive, UPS or electronic loads at their terminals, or link line and neutral together and test only to earth, as the maker allows, and remove or disconnect surge protective devices. Motor cables fed from drives are tested with the cable disconnected from the drive. Afterwards I would reconnect everything as it was, check the connections, and record what was disconnected.
markingPoints: Explains damage risk and false readings from filters and SPDs
Explains stored energy and UPS back-feed
Follows makers' instructions, isolates, waits discharge time and proves dead
Disconnects or protects electronic equipment and SPDs, or tests L+N to earth
Reconnects correctly and records what was disconnected

practical1.title: Dead test a multi-source training installation and complete the schedules
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a training rig that is NOT connected to any supply: a main board feeding a sub-board, a generator inlet with a changeover switch, a dummy PV AC isolator, three-phase and split-phase circuits, an armoured sub-main, a busbar chamber with bolted joints, and a practice earth electrode in the yard. The assessor has planted faults (for example a high-resistance joint, an insulation fault and a reversed polarity). As a group, give each member a role (test lead, two testers, recorder, and safety and isolation lead) and swap so that everyone carries out each kind of test. Write a short test plan and isolation plan listing every source. Isolate and lock off every source with every member's padlock and a tag, and prove dead with a tester checked before and after use. Carry out continuity of protective conductors and the armour, insulation resistance between every pair of conductors, polarity, a micro-ohm (or low-resistance) test across the busbar joints, and a fall-of-potential test on the practice electrode. Record every reading on the schedules, find the planted faults, and write what each one means.
materials: Multi-source training rig with planted faults, not connected to any supply
Practice earth electrode area with room for test spikes
Lock-off kit with a multi-lock hasp, one padlock per member, and tags for every source
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit
Insulation and continuity tester, with its check box
Earth electrode tester with spikes, leads and a measuring tape
Blank test plan, isolation plan and schedules of test results
photos: The written test plan and isolation plan listing every source
Every source locked off with every member's padlock and a tag
The tester checked on the proving unit before and after proving dead
A member taking the micro-ohm reading across a busbar joint
The fall-of-potential set-up with the spikes at their measured distances
The completed schedules with the planted faults marked
checklist: Helped list every source and the order of tests in the plan
Isolated, locked off and proved dead correctly, with the tester checked before and after
Carried out a continuity and an insulation test correctly
Placed the leads correctly for the micro-ohm test
Set out the earth electrode spikes correctly and took the check readings
Recorded real readings clearly on the schedules
Found at least one planted fault and explained what it means
safety: The rig stays dead and locked off throughout; only the instructor ever energises anything
Every source is locked off: mains, generator inlet and PV isolator
Warn others before each insulation test and let the circuit discharge before touching it
Keep people clear of the test spikes and leads in the yard, and check for buried services before driving spikes

practical2.title: Analyse a full set of test results and write the test report
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a results pack for a made-up complex installation (a small hotel in Ocho Rios with a main switchboard, four sub-boards, a generator, a UPS and a PV system), with the design limits as data. The pack holds the dead test results and the live results taken by a competent person: loop impedance on mains and on generator, prospective fault current at each board with the breakers' breaking capacities, RCD trip times, polarisation index readings for two pump motors, micro-ohm readings for the busbar joints, PV string open-circuit voltages and currents with the light level, CT ratio checks and the earth electrode readings. Some results fail. As a group, give each member a role (lead tester, two results analysts, report writer, and presenter) and swap so that every member checks another's work. Check every result against the limits, work out the polarisation indexes and compare the PV strings and busbar joints. List each failure with its likely cause, the action and the retest needed. Complete the schedules and a draft certificate, and write a short test report. Present it to the assessor, who plays the client's engineer.
materials: Results pack for a made-up hotel installation, with design limits (from the assessor)
Blank schedules of test results, a draft certificate form and a report template
Flip chart or whiteboard for the presentation
photos: The results marked pass or fail against the limits
The polarisation index, PV string and busbar comparisons worked out
The list of failures with causes, actions and retests
The completed schedules and draft certificate
The presentation to the client's engineer
checklist: Checked results against the limits correctly
Worked out the polarisation indexes correctly
Spotted the odd PV string and the high busbar joint
Saw that a circuit passes on mains but fails on generator, and said why it matters
Gave a sensible cause, action and retest for each failure
Wrote part of the report clearly and accurately
Explained the findings clearly to the client's engineer
safety: This is a desk and presentation task: no equipment is opened or energised
The report must say that failed circuits stay isolated until they are repaired and retested
Treat the made-up client's information as confidential, as you would on a real job
